name: Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology
short_description: Develop Your Automotive Skills. Drive Your Career Forward.
description: Build practical automotive knowledge and technical skills with the Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology. Learn to inspect, service, diagnose and repair a wide range of light vehicle systems, including engines, brakes, steering, suspension and automotive electrical components.

key_information.duration: Provider-dependent. Duration varies depending on the registered training provider, delivery arrangements and learner experience.
key_information.delivery: As offered by the registered training organisation (RTO). Delivery may include classroom learning, online learning and practical automotive workshop training.
key_information.extent: 36 units of competency: 20 core units and 16 elective units.
key_information.delivery_notification: Study mode, workshop facilities, practical training arrangements, course duration and intake dates vary by registered training provider. Confirm current availability and enrolment requirements directly with the provider.

overview.heading: Build Your Future in the Automotive Industry
overview.description: The AUR30620 Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology is designed for individuals seeking to develop the technical knowledge and practical skills required to work in the automotive service and repair industry.
content: This qualification covers a broad range of automotive activities, including vehicle servicing, engine diagnostics, electrical systems, braking systems, steering, suspension and mechanical repairs.

You will develop the ability to identify vehicle faults, perform diagnostic procedures, use automotive tools and equipment, and carry out repairs in accordance with workplace safety and industry standards.

Whether you are starting your automotive career or looking to have your existing mechanical experience formally recognised, this qualification can support your professional development in the light vehicle automotive sector.

why_choose.heading: Why Choose This Qualification?
why_choose.description: Develop industry-relevant automotive skills, build practical mechanical capabilities and prepare for opportunities across the automotive service and repair industry.

benefits.title: Nationally Recognised Qualification
benefits.description: Gain a nationally recognised automotive qualification that demonstrates your skills and knowledge in light vehicle mechanical servicing and repair.

benefits.title: Develop Practical Mechanical Skills
benefits.description: Build technical capabilities in vehicle maintenance, engine diagnostics, automotive electrical systems, braking and suspension repairs.

benefits.title: Recognition of Prior Learning
benefits.description: Experienced automotive workers may be able to demonstrate existing competency through an RPL assessment supported by relevant workplace evidence.

benefits.title: Expand Your Career Opportunities
benefits.description: Develop the skills required for a range of automotive service, maintenance and mechanical repair roles across the automotive industry.

entry_requirements.heading: What Do You Need to Get Started?

qualification_requirements.title: Entry Requirements
qualification_requirements.description: The official AUR30620 qualification has no formal entry requirements. However, Career Skills Institute Australia may conduct its own enrolment and pre-training checks to understand each learner's needs and suitability for the proposed delivery pathway.
items: Relevant educational or employment information, where applicable.
Participation in a Language, Literacy, Numeracy and Digital Literacy (LLND) assessment.
Access to a computer and internet for online learning, where applicable.
Relevant workplace or automotive experience for Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) applicants.

core_skills.title: Core Skills
core_skills.description: Learners should be prepared to develop and demonstrate the following skills:

items.name: Reading
items.description: Understand automotive manuals, technical instructions, workshop procedures and vehicle specifications.

items.name: Writing
items.description: Complete service reports, maintenance records, repair documentation and workplace forms.

items.name: Numeracy
items.description: Perform measurements, calculations and basic technical assessments relevant to automotive servicing.

items.name: Communication
items.description: Communicate effectively with customers, supervisors and other automotive professionals.

items.name: Digital Skills
items.description: Use computers, diagnostic equipment and digital resources to access technical information and complete learning activities.

course_structure.heading: Course Structure – Explore What You'll Learn
course_structure.description: The AUR30620 Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology consists of 36 units of competency, including 20 core units and 16 elective units.

groups.title: Core Units
groups.description: Mandatory units required for the qualification.

units.title: Follow environmental and sustainability best practice in an automotive workplace
Follow safe working practices in an automotive workplace
Test and repair basic electrical circuits
Diagnose and repair spark ignition engine management systems
Test, charge and replace batteries and jump-start vehicles
Diagnose and repair charging systems
Diagnose and repair starting systems
Diagnose and repair ignition systems
Diagnose and repair light vehicle hydraulic braking systems
Diagnose and repair light vehicle steering systems
Diagnose and repair light vehicle suspension systems
Diagnose and repair light vehicle engines
Diagnose and repair light vehicle emission control systems
Carry out servicing operations
Develop and carry out diagnostic test strategies
Inspect and service braking systems
Diagnose and repair cooling systems
Inspect and service engines
Inspect and service petrol fuel systems
Use and maintain tools and equipment in an automotive workplace

groups.title: Elective Units
groups.description: Elective units selected as part of the qualification to develop additional automotive skills and knowledge.

units.title: Respond to customer needs and enquiries in an automotive workplace
Communicate effectively in an automotive workplace
Repair wiring harnesses and looms
Install basic ancillary electrical systems and components
Apply knowledge of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS)
Diagnose and repair network electronic control systems
Depower and reinitialise battery electric vehicles
Inspect and maintain battery electric vehicles
Service air conditioning and HVAC systems
Carry out light vehicle wheel alignment operations
Remove and install light vehicle engine assemblies
Diagnose and repair light vehicle manual transmissions
Diagnose and repair light vehicle automatic transmissions
Diagnose and repair light vehicle clutch systems
Diagnose and repair engine forced-induction systems
Balance wheels and tyres

items.title: Automotive Servicing and Maintenance
items.description: Develop the ability to perform routine vehicle servicing, inspections and maintenance procedures according to manufacturer specifications.

items.title: Engine Diagnostics and Repairs
items.description: Learn to identify engine faults, perform diagnostic procedures and undertake relevant mechanical repairs on light vehicle engines.

items.title: Automotive Electrical Systems
items.description: Build skills in testing and repairing electrical circuits, batteries, charging systems, starting systems and ignition systems.

items.title: Brake System Inspection and Repair
items.description: Understand how to inspect, service, diagnose and repair light vehicle hydraulic braking systems.

items.title: Steering and Suspension Systems
items.description: Develop knowledge of steering and suspension components, including inspection, fault identification and repair procedures.

items.title: Cooling System Maintenance
items.description: Learn to diagnose cooling system problems and perform relevant servicing and repair procedures.

items.title: Fuel and Emission Control Systems
items.description: Understand petrol fuel systems, engine management and emission control technologies used in modern vehicles.

items.title: Automotive Diagnostic Techniques
items.description: Develop the ability to select diagnostic strategies, use testing equipment and interpret technical information to identify vehicle faults.

items.title: Workshop Safety and Sustainability
items.description: Apply safe work practices, environmental procedures and sustainable practices within an automotive workshop.

items.title: Automotive Tools and Equipment
items.description: Learn to select, operate and maintain automotive tools, equipment and measuring instruments safely and effectively.

career_pathways.heading: Where Can Your Automotive Skills Take You?
career_pathways.description: Completing this qualification may support career opportunities in automotive service and repair environments, depending on experience, employer requirements and demonstrated competency.

items.title: Light Vehicle Mechanic
items.description: Perform routine maintenance, inspections, servicing and mechanical repairs on passenger cars and other light vehicles.

items.title: Automotive Technician
items.description: Use diagnostic tools and technical knowledge to identify vehicle faults and undertake mechanical and electrical repairs.

items.title: Automotive Service Technician
items.description: Carry out scheduled servicing, vehicle inspections and maintenance procedures in automotive service centres.

items.title: Automotive Repair Technician
items.description: Assist with diagnosing mechanical problems and repairing vehicle components and systems.

items.title: Workshop Technician
items.description: Support workshop operations by undertaking servicing, maintenance, inspections and repair tasks.

items.title: Vehicle Maintenance Technician
items.description: Maintain vehicle performance and reliability through inspections, servicing and preventive maintenance activities.
